history.dynasty: Nolamba dynasty (with Western Ganga support); later Hoysala additions
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple at Aralaguppe village in Tiptur taluk, over 1100 years old; its date is confirmed by stone inscriptions (c. 895 CE) and it was built by the Nolamba kings with support from the Western Gangas. 'Kalleshwara' (kallu = stone) signifies Shiva as eternal and unchanging; the main deity is a Shiva Linga. Built in early Dravidian style with Nolamba influence — square sanctum, navaranga with carved doorway (Gajalakshmi on lintel, dwarf rows on pediment), and a famous central ceiling of nine intricately carved panels with Tandaveshvara at the centre surrounded by the Ashtadikpalas and flying Gandharvas. Four other temples of the Ganga period stand in the complex. Aralaguppe is called the 'Museum of Temples'.

name: Kalleshwara Temple
town_description: Aralaguppe is a small village in Tiptur taluk of Tumakuru district, set amid greenery and open fields. It is known as the 'Museum of Temples' for its Kalleshwara and Chennakeshava temples and a cluster of Ganga-period shrines. The village is quiet and rural; most visitors are heritage travellers coming for the stone carvings. (CSV town 'Tumkur' is approximate — the temple is at Aralaguppe, Tiptur Taluk.)

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~150 km, verify)
travel.road: Reachable by road from Tiptur; the village priest or a local guide usually shows visitors around. Karnataka Archaeology Dept coordinates: 13.2535 N, 76.6183 E.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours — the priest is not always present; ask a local resident to open the shrine (verify)
